summary.text: GO: expressed (4.004 TPM in Small_Intestine_Terminal_Ileum, the run's chosen tissue and a disease tissue for this contrast), dysregulated in the study (logFC 2.7, adjusted p 4.2e-20), and a mouse phenotype on record (phenotyped, 2 abnormal terms). Hypothesis: inhibition, because the gene is up-regulated in the Crohn's disease versus non-inflammatory-bowel-disease control contrast, logFC 2.7, adjusted p 4.2e-20. Mouse knockouts show decreased susceptibility to induced arthritis and decreased susceptibility to injury; expression is 4.004 TPM in Small_Intestine_Terminal_Ileum against a median of 5.982 TPM across 54 tissues. Two agents hit this target with 3 of 23 trial rows live, the furthest being the Phase 3 antibody bemarituzumab (none indicated for a disease attributable to this target); development level: an approved drug acts on it, with 37704 PubTator3 records. The change may reflect infiltrating immune cells rather than regulation in the tissue: whole blood 164.1 TPM and spleen 240.9 TPM both exceed the region's 4.004 TPM. No data: chemical probe; the pipeline phase ring is not applicable for this target.
